clean_body: [ ]Adam Schiff for Congress Derek — I was moving some boxes of old junk into the attic recently and found a couple of scrapbooks. One of them included a photo that I just had to share with you from high school. This photo is of me after winning a competition for a speech on America’s free enterprise system, believe it or not. (Leave it to a high school student to opine on the economy whose only relevant experience was working in a restaurant and his father’s lumber yard.) The envelope contained a check for first prize — it was a hundred dollars. That was a lot of money back then. It still is. Just take a look: [ ]Old photo of Adam Schiff during his high school debate years [ ]Before I go on, and I realize this is a different type of email than you’re getting from most campaigns right now, can you pitch in $10 to help fuel my fight to protect our democracy and our House and Senate Majorities? When I was 11 years old, my dad moved our family from Scottsdale, Arizona to the San Francisco Bay Area. I started in a new middle school before attending Monte Vista High School in Danville. I played on the soccer team and had several wonderful teachers who really made a mark on me. There was Mr. Morrison, who taught contemporary world problems; Ms. Shackleford, my calculus teacher; and Mr. Morrison, who taught physiology and had us dissecting fetal pigs — I can still smell the formaldehyde. Ugh. But the two teachers who left the biggest mark on me were Ms. Abbott, my Shakespeare teacher, and Al Gentile, my speech coach. Ms. Abbott took our class up to Oregon each summer for the Shakespeare festival, but it was Mr. Gentile who taught us the art of public speaking. That was the after-school activity that really got me going and I was soon competing in speech tournaments. At first, I wasn’t very good, scoring 5s at tournaments which was, well, the lowest score you could get. I did dramatic interpretation — Twelve Angry Men and Inherit the Wind were a couple of favorites — I loved those plays but ... they didn’t love me. Then I switched to Original Oratory and things started to change. In “OO” you could write your own material, craft a speech on a topic of your own choice, and that made all the difference. Hence the picture before you now. Although speaking before others did not come naturally to me, I worked hard at it, reading great speeches from Lincoln and Frederick Douglass, and listening to recordings of Robert Kennedy, Martin Luther King, Jr., Winston Churchill, John F. Kennedy, and more. I couldn’t get enough. From the tinny phonograph in my bedroom came these wonderful if scratchy recordings of the greatest speakers of the modern era. It was mesmerizing. And from my brother’s room next door, the sounds of Richard Burton, Laurence Olivier and other greats performing Shakespeare. To this day, I draw on them for inspiration when I’m writing a speech. For my core thesis, I gather the elements that I want to weave together from history, the law or Constitution, or, in the case of an investigation, the key pieces of evidence. Perhaps most important, I try to outline the speech I want to give in my head, without the tyranny of a blank page in front of me. Only when I have a good idea of how I want to structure the piece do I sit down to write. Ideally in a comfy chair by the fire. During the first impeachment trial of President Trump, I would take notes on the key elements that I thought should be incorporated into a closing argument for the day. If I didn’t have time to write the closing, I would put numbers next to each of those bullets to put them in some logical order that told a story. And then I would improvise. But occasionally, I had a whole evening to write a closing argument, and there, I waited until my thoughts coalesced around the theme and its most logical order before putting pen to paper, or more accurately — fingers to iPad! Some things never change. But the lessons from those early years — and from those wonderful teachers — have stayed with me: The need to speak plainly, but not dumb down your words. The need to communicate in a way that draws on the inherent beauty of our language, and our higher aspirations and ideals. And the need to appeal to the best in human nature, not the worst. I hope these lessons have helped me be a more effective advocate for our democracy. My parents and teachers taught me that certain very basic values really mattered. That truth matters, that decency matters, and that our democracy matters. And it’s up to each one of us to use the skills we have to fight for them. And it’s why I’m asking you today: [ ]Will you chip in $10 to our campaign to protect our democracy today? | | Folks, we know what the Republicans will do if they regain power. They’re telling us. They’re being straight up about it. They’re going to repeal lower prescription drug prices.
They’re going to cut Social Security and Medicare.
They’ll pass massive tax giveaways for the super-wealthy.

body:
Their analysts say this race will “[come] down to which campaign gets its voters to the polls on or before Election Day.”
#

Meredith College just released **a brand new poll today that shows Cheri Beasley down by just 1 point. That’s well within the margin of error — a statistical dead heat.**
Their analysts say this race will “[come] down to which campaign gets its voters to the polls on or before Election Day.” It’s all about turnout now, and a very small number of votes could make all the difference on Election Day.
Early voting is still happening, and we are aiming for our largest GOTV effort ever this weekend. But there are still investments in organizing that we need to make if we’re going to pull this off.
[**Please contribute $3 or anything you can today. Every dollar will be immediately invested in our organizing efforts today to make sure we reach the voters that Cheri needs to win.**](https://act.cheribeasley.com/go/2567?c0=cb-em-nov22.g3HOlK&refcode=em221101-3-MA&t=1&akid=2198%2E357359%2Eq2y9b2)
Cheri has kept this race tied for months. Outside Republican groups have spent over $63 million to try to take her down and buy this seat for Ted Budd. But we’ve fended off their lies and smears at every turn, and we’re not stopping now.
We will not take a single county or voter for granted — especially when this poll shows that 6 percent remain undecided. It’s those voters that can swing this race to victory.
Less than 1 percent of votes could decide whether we expand the majority so Cheri can cast the decisive vote for progress on climate change, voting rights, codifying Roe, and more.
[**Will you please make a $3 contribution today to keep up our momentum and help us secure a historic victory on Tuesday? It’s clearer than ever that Cheri can win, but she cannot do this alone.**](https://act.cheribeasley.com/go/2567?c0=cb-em-nov22.g3HOlK&refcode=em221101-3-MA&t=2&akid=2198%2E357359%2Eq2y9b2)

body:
I have a history of bipartisan, effective leadership and experience. I'm someone who's not afraid to tackle issues and get things done. | |
---
| | | [ ](https://pennyronning.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=05c2d51066158a4f5219d9967&id=7fc229e9d2&e=2f4ec52c5e)
---
| | | Hello,

We have had FIVE major debates this cycle and many more community events in which we talked about the issues. **Rep. Matt Rosendale could only bother to show up to two of them. In particular, he ignored the debates focused on our farming and Native American communities.**

I have a history of bipartisan, effective leadership and experience. I'm someone who's not afraid to tackle issues and get things done. _**I'm here to represent you!**_

Now, let's win this thing on Nov. 8! Find your [election office here](https://pennyronning.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=05c2d51066158a4f5219d9967&id=ec1288ca7f&e=2f4ec52c5e) and turn in your ballot or vote on election day.
---
| [ ](https://pennyronning.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=05c2d51066158a4f5219d9967&id=436c429517&e=2f4ec52c5e)
---
MTN- Montana's 2nd Congressional District Debate
| | "I am a believer that abortion is healthcare, and whether that's the state government, local/municipal government, or federal government, that any form of government does not have the right and should not have the right to decide what is best for a woman and her body. That should be the choice between that woman and her medical provider over what is the best medical decision." - Penny Ronning
---
| [ ](https://pennyronning.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=05c2d51066158a4f5219d9967&id=a551af1168&e=2f4ec52c5e)
---
Yellowstone Public Radio and Lee Newspapers Debate at MSU Billings
| | "What we're willing to tolerate we will not change. There's a lot about Matt Rosendale that I was not willing to tolerate. He has constantly voted against supporting victims of violent crime, he voted against supporting nursing mothers, and he voted against helping elderly folks that are discriminated against in the workplace." - Penny Ronning
---
| [ ](https://pennyronning.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=05c2d51066158a4f5219d9967&id=9c402f3386&e=2f4ec52c5e)
---
Montana PBS Debate
| | "We 100 percent need to have federal funding coming into our rural communities for childcare. Rural families simply cannot afford this on their own. Our rural communities need help, and I do believe this is something that Congress can address." - Penny Ronning
---
| [ ](https://pennyronning.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=05c2d51066158a4f5219d9967&id=86762d4380&e=2f4ec52c5e)
---
Montana Farmer's Union Debate
| | "So I think that what we need to stop doing is electing millionaires to Congress. They don't live like the rest of us live. They don't live like 95, 96, and 97 percent of Montanans live. We need to start electing Montanans." - Penny Ronning
---
| [ ](https://pennyronning.us11.list-manage.com/track/click?u=05c2d51066158a4f5219d9967&id=37375d6a80&e=2f4ec52c5e)
---

# Portland Press Herald - Letter to the Editor: Weighing all sides, Independent will vote Republican
I grew up during Woodstock and believed we were living in the Age of Aquarius: “Harmony and understanding, sympathy and trust abounding.” I’m an independent and vote Democratic.There’s tremendous murkiness about our common connection as human beings. Many are tired of name calling and fear tactics. We need to talk, respectfully.Something that has bothered me during the last two years has been the censoring of discussion about controversial topics. Science demands “rigorous skepticism.” Respectfully discussing all sides of every topic will help heal humanity.I attended an event this evening and listened to several Republican candidates for office. I was so impressed by the calm demeanor and courageous integrity of the keynote speaker that I’ve decided to give Ed Thelander my vote for Congress on Nov. 8. The other candidates – Amy Arata (House District 104), Jennifer White (Senate District 25) and David Reed (House District 105) – are also emulating these virtues. I’m voting for Arata and White.**Kimberly Brown** _Gray_
|

If you are told by a town clerk or any election official that filling out an RCV ballot across all three columns invalidates your ballot, please call Maine GOP Election Integrity Director Sharon Bemis at (207) 668-6157 immediately.**Please note: The instructions on your ballot will advise you to “fill in no more than one oval for each candidate or column.” HOWEVER, this DOES NOT invalidate your ballot. We advise you to fill in all three ovals in Ed’s column.**[**CLICK this LINK for an INSTRUCTIONAL PDF by the Maine Secretary of State’s Office on how to properly fill out an RCV Ballot.**](https://thelanderforcongress.us5.list-manage.com/track/click?u=035bf0620f01206429344ca39&id=d5bea7563f&e=f8a0a76a2b)****

THE RNC HAS EXTENDED OUR DEADLINE BY 24 HOURS, AS SUCH WE'RE ACTIVATING A 10X MATCH THROUGH MIDNIGHT TONIGHT | [](http://links.alekskarlatosforcongress.com/u/click?_t=7e7d86e0b42141418fdbf0bb715c41e9&_m=6c3c951706e646adb97fd770580e6f2f&_e=98VJONJSoQGo93FnkCp8IOeGfOXhdVnQpqVGP4mqKrRZwprG7hIcDKloSVA0RhLdHSdGs55NnpSK2oeETbFG0wpfIlGSMZllPGpSqQzTRZpMhrSoOxtM032kn6rtWuHQxOSgKrc02IXi0ogcJ1fzCpbLQQcDfaNO5LkXZ9ZRs6d3S4xhe9U78v0StDZDH7ae-2mRB7F0UcJwJzUfNburEaVKL8kdB9nxpEvXdeXNU39lVUhkhahFC8URKkNu24NOnHnhCwee7T9gteRnZApMkpenIzxsstgn8-lOgd7mKqFFwCLTAVX4mRBqTlb_s9gRMKo8w8H4ZxvXIRTVvwEgSrf_EQKWKbEwkROq1mLsrQnyDX6u-wcuEqzpVwnZbUl6Rp8Xgt9cwYqyTUj7x_R2xg%3D%3D)

_**SEVEN DAYS AND IT'S ALL OVER. PLEASE KEEP THIS IN MIND**_

name: AOC Organizing Team
subject: Checking in
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez for Congress
body:
We’re one week out, how are you feeling?
# [](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/143?refcode=em20221101-3558-header&t=1&akid=3558%2E2526796%2E9K2DP4)
We’re officially one week out from Election Day and we get it — emotions are probably running high.
Your inbox is filled to the brim with emails from candidates, you’re seeing new polls pop up every day, and every headline seems to include the phrase, “neck and neck.”
Before we share a few tips on how to get through election week, we want to hear from you. [Will you take our quick Pre-Election Survey to let us know how you’re feeling, what your voting plan is, and if there’s anything you need help with to get out and vote? ](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/survey/pre-election-survey/?source=em20221101-3558-P_ENG_SUR_MIS&t=2&akid=3558%2E2526796%2E9K2DP4)
**[How are you feeling? →](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/survey/pre-election-survey/?source=em20221101-3558-P_ENG_SUR_MIS&t=3&akid=3558%2E2526796%2E9K2DP4)**
Now, here are some tips and reminders to get you through election week.
* Your worries are valid. There’s a lot at stake in this election. We need to work really, really hard because we are still very much at a very critical precipice of fascism in this country. **If you’re feeling stressed, sign up to phone bank for a candidate or chip in to support a candidate like[Summer Lee](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/go/15095?t=4&akid=3558%2E2526796%2E9K2DP4).

**
* **Be intentional about your news intake.** Cable news can be especially fear-mongering, so consider setting some limits or reading articles instead.

* **Polling data is a data point,** but it’s not the end all be all. If anything, it should act as a motivator.

* Make sure your friends and family have a plan to vote. Offer to drive them to the polls, or send them resources about where to vote and what’s on their ballot.

* Lastly, remember that no matter what happens, we have each other's backs and that our movement is stronger than any single election outcome.

[**Do you have other tips to share? Let us know in our Pre-Election Survey here and we’ll collect your tips and share them with others.**](https://act.ocasiocortez.com/survey/pre-election-survey/?source=em20221101-3558-P_ENG_SUR_MIS&t=5&akid=3558%2E2526796%2E9K2DP4)
Happy voting,
Team AOC

**[Donate](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/ocasio-campaign?refcode=em20221101-3558-P_ENG_SUR_MIS&t=6&refcode2=3558_2526796_9K2DP4&akid=3558%2E2526796%2E9K2DP4)** | **[Merch](https://shop.ocasiocortez.com/?utm_source=em-footer-20221101-3558-P_ENG_SUR_MIS&t=7&akid=3558%2E2526796%2E9K2DP4)**

Dear ,

Did you see this email that just came out from the Secretary of the State’s Office? They are already saying to expect a delay in results due to an “increase in absentee ballots,” one week out from the election.

We are expecting 70% fewer absentee ballots in 2022 compared to 2020. There is no reason for the Secretary of the State’s office to scare voters with the promise of delayed results.

What this email is really saying is that our election infrastructure is failing. What we saw during the primary in August were failing machines. I am hearing from officials all over the state that the registration system is constantly down.

It is time for a change. As your next Secretary of the State, I will bring technology to the forefront of our elections. No excuses and no delayed results.

Onward to Election Day!

Thank you and Godspeed,

Dominic Rapini

Republican Candidate for Secretary of the State

[1]Stacey Abrams for Governor

Derek,

We officially have exactly one week left on this campaign. And I wanted to
let you know exactly where your donations will go in the last few days of
this campaign.

But first, I have to be upfront: we have a lot left to do in the final
stretch.

reach before polls close for good in one week. With so little time left,
I’m counting on this grassroots team to dig deeper than ever. Will you
invest $5 right now? Your support can make the difference
in a race that will be decided by the narrowest of
margins,
Derek.

[ https://act.staceyabrams.com/go/6203?refcode=sa_em_221101_B5_Donations_S1_T1_SYA_30open&email=dpwillis67%40gmail.com&zip=&firstname=Derek&lastname=Willis&addr1=&city=&state=&phone=None&employer=&occupation=&amount=5&amounts=5%2C25%2C50%2C100%2C250&t=1003&akid=16625%2E1862389%2EU2k9j5 ]DONATE

With your investment today, we will keep building on the massive turnout
and send shockwaves through the nation on Election Night.

We can get one more ad up on TV, the radio or online. We can send yard
signs to that one extra neighborhood. We can knock one more street of
doors. We can get one more volunteer to speak directly with voters in
their community.

All of that is still possible — but only if you invest today.

More than the tactics that will win this race, though, I want you to know
where you’ve made your investment — who exactly you’re betting on in this
election.

You’re betting on the woman in Savannah who wants to expand her small
business.

On the first-generation college student from Macon who wants to become a
doctor someday.

On the second grader in Augusta who wants to feel as safe in the classroom
as he does at home.

On the mother of three in Atlanta who wants to put a down payment on her
first home.

By making your contribution today, you’re investing in

| | **2022 November e-newsletter**

**Halloween marks beginning of rainy season**
Dear friends,
I hope everyone enjoyed the Halloween weekend and the rain that came down Tuesday. I had a blast with my son Piero at the Colma Recreation Center’s second Trunk-or-Treat and of course at the Serramonte Shopping Center Monday evening when candy galore was being handed out. Piero dressed as the Yoshi character from Mario Bros. fame, by the way.

This is one of my favorite times of the year as the holidays approach and the weather gets cooler. It’s also a reminder that it is flu season and of course we must be mindful that COVID is not over yet. I encourage everyone to get their flu shot and the updated COVID booster if you haven’t done so already. Let’s continue to protect ourselves and our families as we are wrapping up nearly three years of living in a pandemic. To learn more, go to: https://www.smchealth.org/post/covid-19-vaccine-and-booster.

It is also voting season with a week to go before the mid-term elections.

Every registered voter in San Mateo County has received a mail-in ballot and it must be dropped in the mail by Tuesday, Nov. 8. There are also voting centers up and running throughout the county if you want to cast your ballot there. To learn more go to: https://www.smcacre.org/elections/vote-center-and-ballot-drop-box-lookup.
**County commits $4 million annually to prevent evictions**
The San Mateo County Board of Supervisors has approved $4 million annually in funding to support a local voucher program to help keep 100 formerly homeless individuals and families in their permanent homes.
It’s a bold local strategy to reinforce the safety net for the county’s most vulnerable residents by helping to prevent evictions.

The County of San Mateo Housing Voucher Program said the will launch in 2023, according to the County Manager’s Office. The funds will fill the gap between rent paid by formerly homeless individuals and families with extremely low incomes and the actual rent to avoid evictions, according to the County Manager’s Office.

This is in addition to $54.6 million to the county recently committed to build 1,000 units of affordable housing. This brings the total to $254 million the county has committed to housing our most vulnerable residents over the last decade plus.
****
**Celebrating Filipino American History Month**
Since 1988, communities across California and the United States set aside the month of October to recognize the achievements and contributions of Filipinos and Filipino Americans of this country. Did you know that the earliest documented Filipino presence in the continental United States was October 18, 1587, when the first “Luzones Indios” arrived in Morro Bay, California, on board the Nuestra Senora de Esperanza?

The Filipino American National Historical Society recognizes 1763 as the year in which the first permanent Filipino settlement in the United States was established in St. Malo, Louisiana. I’m proud to represent the largest group of Filipino Americans in Daly City and north San Mateo County than just about anywhere in the United States.

In October, I sponsored a proclamation reaffirming San Mateo County’s commitment to strengthen its solidarity with the Filipino American community. The proclamation recognizes the Filipino American community’s impact to the county’s best interests and wellbeing and reaffirms the county’s duty to support their civic engagement and significant contribution to the conversation, action, and future not only in this county but throughout the United States of America.

**MTC prioritizes Caltrain electrification**
****
As a representative serving San Mateo County on the Metropolitan Transportation Commission, I proud to announce the commission last week voted unanimously to adopt a new policy for prioritizing, building and delivering the next generation of major Bay Area transportation projects, including the electrification of Caltrain.

Officially known as the Major Project Advancement Policy (MAP), the new investment framework marks the first overhaul of the Bay Area’s transit expansion policy since 2008. Designed to support implementation of Plan Bay Area 2050, the MAP balances the sequencing of new projects with limited available funding, prioritizing those that already have received significant grants of state or federal dollars and are either now under construction or poised to begin construction soon.

These include the ongoing electrification of the Caltrain corridor between San Jose and San Francisco, BART’s Core Capacity initiative to expand service frequencies through the Transbay Tube linking San Francisco and Oakland, and the extension of BART service from Berryessa/North San Jose through downtown San Jose to a new terminus in Santa Clara.

The MAP also prioritizes projects readying for construction, including a Caltrain extension to the Salesforce Transit Center in downtown San Francisco and the Valley Link Rail Project to connect the Dublin/Pleasanton BART station with communities in San Joaquin County.

The MTC also in October approved $3.83 million go to Caltrain and $1.46 million to SamTrans from the 2021 American Rescue Plan Act and the state’s taxes on fuel and diesel fuel to use for issues around fare coordination and integration between agencies, regional mapping and wayfinding, and accessibility.

**Battling food insecurity **
Food insecurity is a problem some residents may still face as we continue to emerge from the pandemic. Here are some resources residents can access: **CalFresh:**
Is a program for people with low-income who meet federal income eligibility rules and want to add to their budget to put healthy and nutritious food on the table. Website: [https://www.cdss.ca.gov/food-nutrition/calfresh](https://davidcanepa.us1.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a3c7592558e548bc8cc150aa5&id=4166fa7472&e=c0babbc643) Contact: (650) 802-6576, [antorres@smcgov.org](mailto:antorres@smcgov.org) **Daly City Partnership:**
DC Partnership is a local partnership that was formed to guide collaborative efforts and connect our community to services that promote well-being. Check out their website for times and locations. Website: [https://www.dcpartnership.org/covid19/](https://davidcanepa.us1.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a3c7592558e548bc8cc150aa5&id=943b68a338&e=c0babbc643) **Second Harvest Food Bank:**
Second Harvest offers food at various locations throughout San Mateo County listed on its webpage. Website: [https://www.shfb.org/get-food/](https://davidcanepa.us1.list-manage.com/track/click?u=a3c7592558e548bc8cc150aa5&id=c0cb75c541&e=c0babbc643) Contacts: Call (800) 984-3663 or text GETFOOD to (408) 455-5181 **Interns wanted to join our team **

We are looking to add to our great group of interns we are currently working with. If you or someone you know may be interested in applying to my Internship Program, submitting this form is the first step: https://forms.gle/hiKqtn7Rird5vXwB9. You can also reach out to Mike Richardson on my staff directly with any questions at mrichardson@smcgov.org

**Follow the Office on Social Media**
If you want to get more insight into our office please connect with us on social media. It’s also a great way to interact with the office and to get notifications on upcoming events. Click the icons below and like us on Facebook and follow us on Twitter.** ** In friendship, David J. Canepa

body:
North Carolina’s Supreme Court hangs in the balance... | | | | | | | Friend, We are just about a week away from one of the most important elections in American history. **In North Carolina, the leftist Supreme Court majority has embraced woke, un-American policies - but that could all change this November.** The state court is currently 4-3, with Democrats holding the majority, but two strong challengers - Trey Allen and Richard Dietz - could tip the balance this year.
---
[](https://unitedamericanconservatives.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=22432bec7f541233c6007cfc2&id=98758fb77e&e=fdefed58de)
---
Our research shows that some of our nation’s most contentious issues will appear in front of the new court, including cases on:
* Voter ID Laws,
* Voting Rights for Felons,
* Abortion Law,
* And much more!

**We can't afford to have woke judicial activists deciding on any of these cases.** That’s why Fair Courts America was founded. We fight back against woke judicial activism at _every_ level of our judiciary - from the Supreme Court to your local prosecutor.
Rush a donation to Fair Courts America **IN THE NEXT 24 HOURS** to help us protect the courts across the country, including states like North Carolina.
---

And that’s why** Fair Courts America** exists. **Our mission is to fight back against the woke mob’s takeover of our judicial system, from the State Supreme Court to your local prosecutor.**
---
[**LEARN MORE >>**](https://unitedamericanconservatives.us14.list-manage.com/track/click?u=22432bec7f541233c6007cfc2&id=28e679d500&e=fdefed58de)

Whether ready-to-use appliances, specialized distributions or your individual config, with custom images you can create cloud servers that are ideally prepared for their intended purpose from the very first start-up. Managing and using custom images has now become even easier, which means that you can build on the appropriate image in any situation.
\- Images as the base for new cloud servers - Managing custom images in the cloud control panel
Images as the base for new cloud servers
In order for new cloud servers to be available immediately, the operating system is not installed manually (e.g. from a DVD), but instead the root volume is prefilled with an image when a new cloud server is launched and this installation template is then further configured during the initial boot process.
You have been able to import and use your own images for a while now at. This enables you to create virtual servers in no time at all using a different operating system to those provided by us or using software and configurations that are completely adapted to your requirements. Where there are several available image files from distributors or third-party providers, it is often the case that one of them has been specifically optimized for OpenStack environments like at cloudscale.
Managing custom images in the cloud control panel
Managing custom images is now also possible in our web-based cloud control panel. Even if you are not using our API, the CLI or the DevOps tools we support, such as Terraform and Ansible, you can now import your own images at n order to start one or more virtual servers on this base. In addition, it is now possible to import images directly in QCOW2 format without needing to convert them to RAW first. It goes without saying that you also benefit from this simplified process if you continue to import images via API.
We recommend that you use `cloud-init` [1] for your own images, too. Using cloud-init, virtual servers can apply numerous settings automatically during the boot process, e.g. relating to the name and IP address of the server. You can also hand over many other options to cloud-init as "user data" at the time you create the server. In addition, you can specify for each custom image how our system should handle the user data. This is of particular significance if your image uses Ignition, which serves a similar purpose, rather than cloud-init. You will find further details about this in the documentation at [2].
Whether you are compiling a customized image with your preferred tools and settings or using a comprehensive complete package from a third-party provider, managing and using your custom images has now become even easier at

Team, First, thank you for the outpouring of support ahead of yesterday’s last end-of-month deadline. It’s always incredibly heartwarming to see how many folks are in our corner and part of this movement. **Today, we are just one week away from Election Day.** But the truth is, the election is happening right now. Marylanders are casting their ballots by mail and voting early in-person. We’re truly running out of time before polls close next Tuesday and this race is over. But I am so hopeful for what will come next: a state with leaders committed to creating pathways to work, wages, and wealth for all, who will leave no one behind. I am ready to listen and fight for you. Looking back, we have built one of the biggest, most diverse coalitions this state has ever seen. From labor unions, to environmental organizations, to our teachers and firefighters, to faith groups, to local, state, and national leaders like President Barack Obama — and thousands of Marylanders from the Western Mountains to the Eastern Shore and everywhere in between. Over the past year and few months, this amazing team and supporters like you have worked so hard to get where we are today. We started by polling in the single digits in our extremely competitive primary race, and ultimately became the official Democratic nominees for governor and lieutenant governor. Our momentum hasn’t stopped since. **[Let’s keep that momentum going through these final seven days until the polls close.
